The concerns of a student using a legal (or illegal) weapon on campus are pretty much unfounded IMO. The real danger is from non-students, who don't care about school policy anyway. For some perspective, I went to university in Newark, NJ, a city riddled with violent crime. We had armed cops all over campus. Very few people in NJ can legally carry, so none of the students did. There were muggings and assaults from thugs in the surrounding areas ALL THE TIME. I just went back through my old university e-mail and pulled up all the safety alerts to write this reply. There was one guy who was going into campus bathrooms and mugging students who came in to use them, at gunpoint. He did this for four months before I stopped getting notifications. There were also several sexual assaults on or near campus. The emails stated whether the perp was a student or "non-affiliate." There was one, ONE, incident of student committed violence, and it was not with a weapon. There were just over 60 incidents total, so just over once per month someone was attacked on or adjacent to campus by "non-affiliates," almost always with a weapon. That does not include stuff that happened a few blocks away, such as at the train station.

I myself was assaulted 3 times during the time I attended, walking to/from the train station. I pulled a weapon once to defend myself. I carried that concealed weapon everyday, in violation of campus policy and NJ law, and I'm glad I did. I wasn't the only one, either.

Understand that I was never concerned by the possibility a school shooting. They are so incredibly rare as to almost be nonexistent. I was, however, quite reasonably concerned by the random violence caused by thugs and criminals. A ban on campus carry doesn't just ban guns on campus; it stops students from protecting themselves to and from campus as well. And, as I showed, we had a strong armed security presence, but that wasn't enough to deter all the crime.
